slides.0.title: Regulations and labels
slides.0.subtitle: The IG / DOC system and the rules for variety and vintage labelling
slides.1.title: The 1999 legal framework
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Law No. 25.163
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The 1999 law on origin, overseen by the National Institute of Viticulture (INV); geographical indications can be defined down to the sub-region level
slides.1.highlights.1.title: IP: Indicación de Procedencia
slides.1.highlights.1.content: For table and regional wines only; at least 80% of the wine must come from grapes produced and made in the named area
slides.1.highlights.2.title: IG: Indicación Geográfica
slides.1.highlights.2.content: A delimited area no larger than a province or an already recognised inter-provincial zone; reserved for quality wines whose character is mainly due to origin
slides.1.content: Argentina's origin system has three tiers — IP, IG and DOC — from loose to strict.
slides.2.title: DOC: the strictest tier
slides.2.highlights.0.title: What DOC requires
slides.2.highlights.0.content: A defined boundary, permitted varieties, maximum yield, minimum vine age, training and density, minimum ageing including oak, and tasting-panel approval (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The current DOCs
slides.2.highlights.1.content: There are 2, both in Mendoza: Luján de Cuyo and San Rafael; in 2022 only Luján de Cuyo was actually used (Argentina.gob.ar)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Differing dates
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Sources date the start of Luján de Cuyo as 1989, 1991 (OIV recognition) or 1993, so years are not tested
slides.2.content: DOC is the choice of a few areas; in practice most wines still use an IG.
slides.3.title: Other label rules
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Variety and origin percentages
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Wines of Argentina says a named variety must be at least 85% and a named origin at least 85% from that place; older sources have 100% or 80% — check the INV text
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Reserva and Gran Reserva
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Reds: Reserva at least 12 months in barrel, Gran Reserva at least 24; whites at least 6 and 12 months (Wines of Argentina)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: How many IGs
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Wines of Argentina lists 101 approved IGs (the article is undated and the number changes)
slides.3.content: Percentages differ between sources, so check the INV text before an exam.
